subject: English Language
title: Conjunctions
introduction: Join ideas clearly, then practise five questions at a time.

rules.title: Join ideas and show meaning
rules.body: And adds; but or although contrasts; because gives a reason; so that shows purpose. Use because before a clause and because of before a noun phrase.
rules.example: She stayed home because she was ill. · Although she was ill, she studied.

rules.title: Time, place and condition
rules.body: When, while, until and as soon as tell us about time. Wherever refers to place. If introduces a condition; unless means if not.
rules.example: Wait until I return. · Unless you hurry, you will miss the bus.

rules.title: Paired conjunctions
rules.body: Use either…or and neither…nor as pairs. Keep the joined parts in the same grammatical form.
rules.example: She will choose either pasta or noodles. · Neither Ravi nor Meera was late.

rules.title: The inversion pairs
rules.body: After no sooner, use than. After hardly, scarcely or barely, use when. These often use inverted word order.
rules.example: No sooner had I arrived than it rained. · Hardly had I arrived when it rained.

worked.prompt: The road was slippery. The driver managed to control the car.
worked.answer: Although the road was slippery, the driver managed to control the car.
worked.explanation: Although shows that the second event happened despite the first.

questions.prompt: The road was slippery. The driver managed to control the car.
questions.answer: Although the road was slippery, the driver managed to control the car.
questions.explanation: Use a suitable connector while keeping the original meaning. Do not use and, but or so.

questions.prompt: The book is fascinating. It contains several historical illustrations.
questions.answer: The book, which contains several historical illustrations, is fascinating.
questions.explanation: Use a suitable connector while keeping the original meaning. Do not use and, but or so.

questions.prompt: You must apologise. The teacher will not forgive your mistake.
questions.answer: Unless you apologise, the teacher will not forgive your mistake.
questions.explanation: Use a suitable connector while keeping the original meaning. Do not use and, but or so.

questions.prompt: You eat too much. You will feel sick.
questions.answer: If you eat too much, you will feel sick.
questions.explanation: Use a suitable connector while keeping the original meaning. Do not use and, but or so.

questions.prompt: The chef will prepare pasta. The chef will prepare noodles.
questions.answer: The chef will prepare either pasta or noodles.
accepted: Either the chef will prepare pasta or noodles.
questions.explanation: Use a suitable connector while keeping the original meaning. Do not use and, but or so.

questions.prompt: The detective found no evidence at the crime scene. He found no witnesses to the incident.
questions.answer: The detective found neither evidence at the crime scene nor witnesses to the incident.
questions.explanation: Use a suitable connector while keeping the original meaning. Do not use and, but or so.

questions.prompt: The athlete crossed the finish line. The crowd began cheering immediately.
questions.answer: Hardly had the athlete crossed the finish line when the crowd began cheering.
questions.explanation: Use a suitable connector while keeping the original meaning. Do not use and, but or so.

questions.prompt: The principal announced the results. The students started celebrating immediately.
questions.answer: No sooner had the principal announced the results than the students started celebrating.
questions.explanation: Use a suitable connector while keeping the original meaning. Do not use and, but or so.

questions.prompt: The weather was very cold. The children continued playing outside.
questions.answer: Although the weather was very cold, the children continued playing outside.
questions.explanation: Use a suitable connector while keeping the original meaning. Do not use and, but or so.

questions.prompt: The shopkeeper did not have the blue dress. He did not have the green dress.
questions.answer: The shopkeeper had neither the blue dress nor the green dress.
questions.explanation: Use a suitable connector while keeping the original meaning. Do not use and, but or so.

questions.prompt: ___ you work carefully, you may make avoidable mistakes.
We stayed indoors ___ the storm had passed.
questions.explanation: Until marks the end of a period.

questions.prompt: ___ the bell rang, the pupils entered the hall immediately.
questions.explanation: As soon as shows immediate sequence.

questions.prompt: ___ he was exhausted, he completed the race.
The library closed early ___ the librarian was ill.
I shall call you ___ I reach home.
___ you travel, carry your identity card.
questions.explanation: Wherever means in any place that.

questions.prompt: She spoke softly ___ the baby could sleep.
He read quietly ___ his sister practised the piano.
You may choose ___ tea or coffee.
Neither the captain ___ the coach was satisfied.
No sooner had the show begun ___ the lights went out.
Hardly had I sat down ___ the telephone rang.
She is taller ___ her older sister.
We could not go out ___ it was raining heavily.
questions.explanation: Because is followed by a clause.

questions.prompt: We could not go out ___ the heavy rain.
questions.explanation: Because of is followed by a noun phrase.

questions.prompt: ___ you leave now, you will catch the train.
We waited ___ the teacher returned.
questions.explanation: Until marks the end of waiting.

questions.prompt: ___ it was late, they continued studying.
He took notes ___ he would remember the details.
I will read ___ you prepare dinner.
You may go ___ you wish.
She opened the door ___ the bell rang.
questions.explanation: As soon as shows an immediate action.

questions.prompt: He remained calm ___ everyone else panicked.
___ you finish your work, you may leave.
___ had we reached the station than the train arrived.
___ had the rain stopped when the players returned.
You can ___ revise now or practise tomorrow.
___ my brother nor my sister likes the film.
Wait here ___ I come back.
questions.explanation: Until marks the time when waiting ends.
